reason: Rank the four-step K-loop unroll first: it is distinct from the measured two-step version, and fewer loop branches are a testable hypothesis, though added code and scheduling pressure are risks. Next, try the tiled NEON transpose with TB. It changes the timed conversion after the TB call lost all but two paired runs, but those results do not show that transpose cost caused the loss. The 64 KiB scratch proposal adds packing and changes traversal; its likely costs and similarity to an unpromoted traversal lower its priority. The 288-byte scratch stride is distinct from the rejected 272-byte layout, but cache benefit is unknown and it adds 16 KiB. TA adds a timed B transpose while retaining both generated packing operations, so its expected costs are substantial. Fused transpose repeats the A transpose across 16 column panels, making its stated 16-fold work a significant risk. Rank the four-tile K-pair proposal last: it appears to alias the already measured two-step unroll unless its actual instruction schedule differs. No proposal has measured evidence of a gain in this batch; ranking expresses test priority, not selection or performance fact.
